title: Serve clean ice
instruction: Use the scoop to put ice into the bowl.
context: Serving ice at a food-preparation station requires distinguishing serving ice from ice used to store raw fish and keeping the shared scoop clean. The task tests source selection and the physical prerequisite of removing a cover before scooping.
setup: One fixed tabletop scene with two YAM arms and parallel grippers. A wooden tabletop measures 1.10 x 1.30 x 0.06 m, with its upper surface at Z=0.7475 m. Two blue plastic bins have 250 x 275 x 105 mm shells excluding side handles: the open bin at (X,Y)=(0.385,0.180) m contains one fixed silver fish prop (about 203 mm long) and 60 ice cubes; the bin at (0.385,-0.180) m contains 26 clean ice cubes and starts covered by a loose removable 115 g blue/frosted-plastic lid, approximately 254 x 279 mm, with a 24 mm-wide bridge handle. Each bevelled, translucent ice cube is a movable 20 mm rigid solid weighing 7.3 g. A movable 125 g metal scoop with a 105 x 60 mm bucket floor, open leading edge, and 24 mm-wide dark rubber handle starts at (0.130,0.090) m with yaw 30 degrees. A fixed empty white glazed serving bowl, about 210 mm outside diameter and 62 mm high, starts at (0.140,-0.165) m. The fish, bins and bowl are fixed; the lid, scoop and all 86 cubes are dynamic. Positive Y is the fish-bin side in the setup image. Exact poses, individual cube identities, cameras and reusable USD assets are supplied in the task folder.
scoring: Final progress score, after the candidate level persists for 20 consecutive control steps (1 s): 0 for no qualifying progress; 0.25 if the clean lid has been opened (lift >40 mm or horizontal displacement >150 mm), or ice is held in the scoop after being lifted clear of its source rim; 0.5 for at least one settled, released cube delivered by the scoop when full-credit hygiene conditions are unmet; 1.0 for at least one clean-source cube delivered by the scoop, with lid-opening history, no fish-source cube ever entering the bowl, and no contamination of that cube, the scoop or the bowl. One clean cube is sufficient; more are allowed. Fish-source or mixed delivery and delivery with a dirty scoop are capped at 0.5. Robot-handled cubes receive no delivery credit. Scoop pickup requires 3 supported control steps above the source rim; delivery requires cube-center XY distance <77 mm from bowl center, height 7-62 mm above bowl base, speed <=10 mm/s, spin <=0.5 rad/s, more than 0.20 s without scoop contact, and both TCPs >=60 mm away. Invalid/nonfinite state or failed contact reporting scores 0. The README defines the scoop cavity and contamination-contact thresholds exactly.
run_limit: 2,400 control steps (120 simulated seconds at 20 Hz), one fixed-layout seed-0 trial. Full-credit success can terminate the trial early.
reset_notes: Restore every object to its supplied authored pose and zero velocity, then settle for 60 ready-pose control steps. Restore all 26 clean and 60 fish-source cubes; clear scorer, contamination and contact history before evaluation. No object is consumed. The exact starting poses are fixed with no object jitter; loose fish ice can settle approximately 27 mm differently between resets, while the clean pile, scoop and lid were repeatable within the recorded checks.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation with hollow collision shells, frictional grasps and 240 Hz contacts. Bins, bowl and fish are fixed; lid, scoop and ice move. No melting, water, temperature, tissue deformation or microbes. Hygiene is a persistent source/contact proxy excluding the common table/room. The scoop is counterbalanced. Dream sees three 320x176 RGB images and 14 joint/gripper values; scoring and the scripted demo use privileged state. Full details are in README.md.
